title: The Aim of Pleasing God
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Aim of Pleasing God
subpoints: The Christian life is motivated by the desire to please Christ.
This aim applies to both the present life and the afterlife.
To please God is to think, believe, and act in ways acceptable to Him.

outline.title: Pleasing God and Doing All for His Glory
subpoints: Pleasing God is synonymous with doing all things to His glory.
The glory of God represents His weight, worthiness, and essence.
God’s glory is revealed in His attributes and character.

outline.title: The Revelation of God’s Glory
subpoints: Moses and Isaiah encountered God’s glory by seeing who He is.
The glory of the Lord filled the temple, prompting worship.
Encountering God’s glory leads to humility and total dedication.

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro explores the central aim of the Christian life as presented in 2 Corinthians 5:9: to be well-pleasing to the Lord. He emphasizes that this aim is not merely a behavioral goal but the fundamental motivation and purpose of existence, applying to both the believer's time on earth and their eternal state. The pastor explains that to please God is to align one's thoughts, beliefs, and actions with what is acceptable to Him, a concept frequently highlighted by the Apostle Paul throughout the New Testament.

The message further connects the act of pleasing God with the broader biblical mandate to do all things for His glory. By examining the Hebrew concept of *kabod* (glory) as weight and worthiness, the sermon illustrates that God's glory is the manifestation of His essential character and attributes. This is seen in the Old Testament accounts of Moses and Isaiah, who, upon encountering the fullness of God's glory, responded with profound humility and worship.

Ultimately, the sermon calls the congregation to recognize that the pursuit of God's pleasure is the driving force behind the Christian walk. It is a call to live with a whole-person purpose, where every aspect of life is directed toward displaying the worthiness of God, leading to a life of consistent devotion and reverence.

In the end, the Christian life is not a collection of disconnected duties, but a single all-encompassing ambition to please the Lord by displaying his glory in everything we do. From the smallest, most ordinary acts like eating or drinking to the most significant decisions we face, our lives are meant to declare the truth about who God is as revealed in Jesus Christ. We were created for his glory, redeemed by his Son, and now we live as visible testimonies of his character in the world. Therefore, let every thought, every choice, every action be governed by this aim, not the pursuit of self, not the assertion of our rights, but the humble, joyful pursuit of making God known.
